purpose: Maps content artifact types to the discipline rubrics a review panel should judge them against. The panel loads the rubric(s) for the artifact's type, scores each criterion 1-10, and the coordinator synthesizes.

audio-drama.note: A full audio drama is judged on its mix, its story, the voice performances, and character consistency.

narration-voiceover.note: A narration VO is judged on delivery + basic audio health (subset of mix criteria apply).

video-visuals.note: A video is judged on cinematography, its narrative (if story-led), and audio if present.

clip-short.note: Short clips judged on visual craft + audio quality (hook/pacing criteria come from the clip stage-spec, applied by the panel).

script.note: A script is judged on story structure + spoken-delivery readiness.

character-bible.note: A character bible/sheet is judged on the character-design rubric.

review_protocol.independence: Judges score independently, never seeing each other's scores until aggregation
review_protocol.aggregation: Robust (geometric median preferred; disagreement = escalate to human)
review_protocol.knowledge_grounding: Each judge receives the artifact + the rubric JSON (criteria with corpus numbers), NOT generic instructions
review_protocol.diagnosis_requirement: Any criterion scored < 7 must produce a specific diagnosis citing the violated corpus rule + a concrete fix
review_protocol.learning_connection: Recurring low-scored criteria across artifacts become proposed policy rules in the self-iteration engine policy store (human approves)
